extracted.intended_audience: registered patent practitioners, USPTO Office of Enrollment & Discipline staff, and counsel involved in practitioner discipline
extracted.subtask_description: Standards, procedures, and sanctions governing disciplinary proceedings for practitioners registered to practice before the USPTO, including misconduct definitions, settlement-agreement requirements, mitigating/remedial factors, and typical sanctions (e.g., public reprimand and publication).

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation to maintain complete records of client funds (37 C.F.R. § 10.112(c)(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioners must maintain complete records of client funds. The Final Order cites violation of 37 C.F.R. § 10.112(c)(3) for not maintaining complete records of client funds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples and guidance in the order: maintaining a separate bank account for client funds and keeping formal accounting records. Anti-pattern: billing and receiving funds only after performing services and not maintaining a separate client funds account or formal accounting records.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on conduct involving returned checks (37 C.F.R. §§ 10.23(b)(4) and 10.23(b)(6))
rubrics_metrics.description: Submitting checks that are returned for insufficient funds violates professional rules (here identified as 37 C.F.R. §§ 10.23(b)(4) and 10.23(b)(6)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Concrete example from the case: Respondent signed and submitted ten checks to the Office that were returned for insufficient funds (totaling $4,073). Such conduct is actionable misconduct. Remediation (making good on returned checks and fees) is a relevant post-violation fact but does not negate the misconduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability of USPTO Disciplinary Rules to registered practitioners (37 C.F.R. § 10.20 et seq.)
rubrics_metrics.description: Attorneys registered to practice before the USPTO are subject to the Disciplinary Rules (37 C.F.R. § 10.20 et seq.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The order states Respondent is a registered patent attorney and thus subject to those rules. Practitioners should consult the cited regulations for specific obligations and prohibited conduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Jurisdictional basis for disciplinary proceedings (35 U.S.C. § 2(b)(2)(D) and 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.20(a)(3), 11.26)
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO Director has jurisdiction over practitioner disciplinary matters pursuant to statutory and regulatory provisions (35 U.S.C. § 2(b)(2)(D) and 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.20(a)(3) and 11.26).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These provisions authorize the Director (or designate) to approve settlement agreements and issue final orders resolving disciplinary complaints. Parties may submit Proposed Settlement Agreements for Director approval under § 11.26.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirements and effect of Proposed Settlement Agreement (37 C.F.R. § 11.26)
rubrics_metrics.description: A Proposed Settlement Agreement must set forth stipulated facts, legal conclusions, and sanctions, and satisfy the requirements of 37 C.F.R. § 11.26; upon approval it resolves the disciplinary action arising from the stipulated facts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The order explains that the OED Director and Respondent submitted a Proposed Settlement Agreement that 'sets forth certain stipulated facts, legal conclusions, and sanctions' and that the Agreement 'resolves all disciplinary action... arising from the stipulated facts.' Settlement agreements are subject to Director approval and become the basis for the Final Order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sanctions that may be imposed and publication/notice requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Sanctions include public reprimand, publication of the Final Order, publication of a Notice of Reprimand in the Official Gazette, and notification to disciplinary enforcement agencies and courts where the practitioner is admitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In this matter the agreed discipline included: (a) public reprimand; (b) publication of the Final Order; (c) publication of a Notice in the Official Gazette containing the practitioner's name, registration number, violations, and corrective actions; and (d) notice of public discipline and reasons to state disciplinary agencies, courts, and the public. The order also references posting decisions in the OED Reading Room.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allocation of costs in settlement
rubrics_metrics.description: The settlement-agreement terms can specify how costs are allocated; in this case each party bears its own costs incurred to date and in carrying out the agreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parties negotiating settlements should expressly state cost allocation (e.g., each party bears its own costs, or respondent pays certain fees). This term was included as part of the agreed-upon discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mitigating factors relevant to discipline determination
rubrics_metrics.description: Factors that may mitigate discipline include length of registration and lack of prior disciplinary history, as well as remediation steps taken by the respondent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The order cites that Respondent had been a registered patent attorney for over 50 years and had no prior disciplinary history; these facts were treated as mitigating and reflected in the agreed discipline. Remedial acts (see next entry) also inform sanction decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remedial steps that bear on discipline (restitution, CLE, establishing client accounts)
rubrics_metrics.description: Post-violation remedial actions that are material to sanctioning include making good on returned checks and fees, completion of continuing legal education on law office management/bookkeeping/ethics, and establishing/maintaining a separate bank account for client funds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This case lists specific remedial steps taken by Respondent: (a) reimbursement of all returned checks and fees; (b) completion of a six-hour CLE on law office management (including bookkeeping and ethics); and (c) establishment and operation of a separate client funds bank account. Such steps may be treated as mitigating and are appropriate corrective practices for practitioners to adopt.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content and public posting of Notice of Reprimand
rubrics_metrics.description: A Notice of Reprimand must identify the practitioner, cite the violated regulations, describe the conduct (including factual details such as dates and amounts), set out remedial steps and mitigating facts, and is to be published (e.g., in the Official Gazette and posted to OED Reading Room).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The order reproduces the Notice of Reprimand wording used for publication: it includes the practitioner's name and registration number, the cited regulatory violations, a factual narrative (business practice, lack of separate account, returned checks and totals), corrective steps taken, mitigating factor(s), and a statement that the action results from a settlement agreement under the cited authorities.
